thread:
maya: quick note: ran a focused ablation on normalization + whitening for launchpad-v0 on product-holdout. results worth discussing.

anya: nice. what's the ablation matrix?

maya: tried: no-norm, l2 postnorm, unit-scaling (mean-centering + scale to std=1), and full PCA-whiten (k=128). each run used fp32 vectors.

kai: top numbers?

maya: product R@1: no-norm=0.412, l2=0.424, unit-scaling=0.431, pca-whiten=0.439. baseline heron-v2 fp32=0.463. so whitening helps most but still -0.024 absolute.

derek: interesting that whitening helps. what about short-query vs long-tail split?

maya: short-query: no-norm=0.502, l2=0.513, whiten=0.533. long-tail: no-norm=0.341, l2=0.365, whiten=0.378. whitening reduces gap but not eliminate.

eval-bot: regression summary: launchpad-v0 whiten vs heron-v2: R@1 delta -0.024, silhouette improved +0.03 vs no-norm. Note: whitening introduces extra CPU preprocessing. Cost estimate: +2-3ms per request at p99 for route.

anya: can we push whitening into model-serving runtime (one-shot mul) to avoid CPU overhead?

derek: potential yes if we bake PCA matrix into postproc kernel (GPU) but need to test numerics and memory for batch sizes.

kai: also maybe do a small-ft where we add whitened variant during training augmentation so model learns whitened distribution.

maya: FYI i also tried combining whiten + l2 and got small further boost (+0.006).

anya: OK operational plan: 1) prototype GPU-side whitening in runtime (eng-runtime), 2) test numeric parity with CPU whitening (maya/kai), 3) if parity, canary route with whiten-on-serve for product traffic. owners: anya infra, derek model + training, maya evals.

maya: i'm uploading the ablation notebook + p99 latency estimates to s3. link: https://redwood-internal/s3/evals/launchpadv0/1771002222/whiten_ablation.html

eval-bot: upload complete.

maya: will re-run after derek's training experiments. thanks all. :sparkles:
